objective: Prove, for hub-free parity laws: (1) bond distance between e and f is the least boundary, counting seams and open ends inside, of a connected region with e and f on its boundary and a connected outside; (2) a region with no open ends inside and a single seam pins that seam, so no knot crosses it and greedy closing breaks space into frozen cells; (3) a connected region whose boundary has b distinctions bonds any two of them at bond distance at most b - 1, so a long strip of bounded cross-section with no open ends inside collapses; (4) the rule 'grow at a knot holding two or more open ends' grows exactly the two-way thread, whose bond distance is the number of knots on the path plus one: a native ruler of dimension one.
status: Proved (OPEN-END-GROWTH-20261107-001B-P001): bond distance is a boundary. In hub-free parity laws the least knot through two distinctions is the least two-sided boundary (seams plus open ends held inside); a region with no open ends behind one seam pins it and no knot crosses (closing every open end seals space into frozen cells), two seams tie but do not decouple; every two-sided boundary is a knot, so long regions with short boundaries are shortcuts (closed strips collapse); growing only at knots holding two open ends grows exactly the two-way thread, a native logical number line.
title: Bond distance is a boundary
